decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit sits at the core of the firm's airfield lighting business and was strongly promoted as a new industry standard, so it likely meets aspirations despite the COVID downturn.
The surveillance display extends the tower offer and was given a page of its own, but the post-COVID loss of slack makes this less central line somewhat vulnerable.
The training program costs little to maintain and supports service revenue across the installed base, so it needs little slack to carry.
The airfield ground lighting course complements the core lighting business at low cost, although it was only mentioned and given low prominence.
The collaboration software fits the firm's strategic move toward integrated, data-driven operations, which justifies carrying it through the downturn even with uncertain results.

The multilateration system is a capital-intensive surveillance offer facing weak airport investment after COVID, but it was launched recently and prominently, so the firm likely keeps it for the recovery.
